title: MySQL: Decode execution of prepared statement with query attributes
description:
The packet for the execution of prepared statements changes slightly if query attributes are enabled.

https://dev.mysql.com/doc/dev/mysql-server/latest/page_protocol_com_stmt_execute.html

Here is a capture from MySQL Server 8.4.0 and MySQL Connector/Python 8.4.0

[prepared_mysql840_connpy.pcapng](/uploads/43246072b74169484b72e455a56d1ae3/prepared_mysql840_connpy.pcapng)

```python
#!/bin/python3
import mysql.connector

c = mysql.connector.connect(
    host='127.0.0.1',
    user='root',
    database='test',
    ssl_disabled=True
)

cur = c.cursor(prepared=True)
cur.execute('SELECT * FROM t1 WHERE 1=%s', (1, ))
for r in cur:
    print(r)

cur.close()

c.close()
```

In a malicious trace, this can presumably overflow since a FLE can have a 64-bit length. That issue already existed before this change, but this adds another case.

Perhaps worth fixing this in the future. I wonder if fuzzing would also reveal infinite loops or worse.
